question_text: Find the derivative of sec 3x from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what you turn sec into, and which identity handles the numerator.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. sec 3(x + h) is sec(3x + 3h). Expand the inside angle before anything else happens.

recall.must_convey: That the first principle is written with f(x) = sec 3x and the angle expanded as 3x + 3h.
accept: write the first principle for sec three x
substitute x plus h so the angle is three x plus three h
take the limit of sec three x plus three h minus sec three x over h
first principle rasi three x plus three h ani rasta
start from the definition of the derivative

steps.why: The definition earns the mark, and expanding 3(x + h) at once means the identity in the next step can be applied to angles that are already written out.
common_mistakes: Quoting 3 sec 3x tan 3x from the standard table, which earns nothing on a first-principle question.
steps.memory_tip: The inside angle triples with x: 3(x + h) = 3x + 3h.

steps.label: Write sec as 1/cos
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Taking reciprocals swaps the order on top: 1/p − 1/q = (q − p)/pq, so cos 3x now comes first in the numerator.
lines: Dividing by h, the denominator becomes

recall.must_convey: That sec is written as 1/cos and the two fractions combined, leaving cos 3x − cos(3x + 3h) on top.
accept: write sec as one by cos and take a common denominator
one by p minus one by q is q minus p over p q so the order flips
the numerator becomes cos three x minus cos three x plus three h
sec ni one by cos ga rasi common denominator teesukovali
combine the two reciprocals into one fraction

steps.why: sec has no addition formula of its own. Written as 1/cos it becomes an ordinary difference of fractions, and the top is then a difference of cosines that the standard identity handles.
common_mistakes: Keeping the order cos(3x + 3h) − cos 3x on top after taking reciprocals, which flips the sign of the answer.
Writing 1/cos A − 1/cos B as 1/(cos A − cos B).
steps.memory_tip: Taking reciprocals swaps the order on top: 1/p − 1/q = (q − p)/pq.

steps.label: Use cos C − cos D
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The half difference is −3h/2, and sin(−3h/2) = −sin(3h/2). That second minus cancels the minus in front of the identity, so the numerator ends up positive.
lines: cos C − cos D = −2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((C−D)/2)

recall.must_convey: That cos C − cos D = −2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((C−D)/2) is applied and the numerator becomes 2 sin(3x + 3h/2) sin(3h/2).
accept: apply cos minus cos to get minus two sin half sum sin half difference
the half difference is minus three h by two so the sign flips back
the numerator becomes two sin of three x plus three h by two into sin three h by two
sin of minus theta is minus sin theta kabatti sign marchipothundi
use the cos minus cos identity on the numerator

steps.why: A difference of two cosines becomes a product only through this identity, and only a product can be separated into a standard limit and a factor that is continuous at h = 0.
common_mistakes: Ignoring sin(−3h/2) = −sin(3h/2) and finishing with the wrong sign.
steps.memory_tip: cos minus cos: minus two, sine of the half sum, sine of the half difference. Sine is an odd function, so a negative half difference flips the sign back.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. sin 3x/cos²3x is split as (1/cos 3x)(sin 3x/cos 3x) to reach the sec-tan form the answer key uses.
lines: As h → 0 that second factor → 1, so

recall.must_convey: That the standard limit is matched by writing (sin(3h/2))/h as (3/2)(sin(3h/2))/(3h/2), and the answer is 3 sec 3x tan 3x.
accept: multiply and divide by three h by two to use the standard limit
the answer is three sec three x tan three x
sin three x over cos squared three x is sec three x tan three x
three sec three x tan three x vasthundi
derivative of sec three x is three sec three x tan three x
heard_as: three sec three x tan three x

steps.why: The 2 from the identity and the 3/2 from matching the standard limit multiply to 3, which is the derivative of the inside angle 3x. Both factors have to be tracked or the 3 is lost.
common_mistakes: Losing the 3/2 needed to match the standard limit and giving 2 sec 3x tan 3x.
Stopping at 3 sin 3x/cos²3x, which is right but not in the expected form.
steps.memory_tip: sec differentiates to sec times tan, with the inside multiplier in front: 3 sec 3x tan 3x.

insider_note: Write both secants as reciprocals and combine over one denominator, which turns the top into cos 3x − cos(3x + 3h). The 3 from the inner function appears twice over.
